topics.label: Introduction and lecture learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the lecture topic and outlines the key learning objectives.

topics.label: Cancer etiology: intrinsic mutations, environment, and epidemiology
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the foundational concepts of cancer etiology, contrasting intrinsic mutational processes and bad luck with environmental exposures and epidemiological patterns.

topics.label: Infectious pathogens as drivers of oncogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe how infectious pathogens drive oncogenesis, focusing in depth on the etiology and mechanism of Burkitt lymphoma.

topics.label: Chemical and physical mutagens and metabolic activation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the biochemical and physical mechanisms by which environmental mutagens and their metabolic derivatives induce DNA damage.

topics.label: Tumor promotion, host susceptibility, and mechanism synthesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the role of non-mutagenic tumor promoters, chronic inflammation, and host developmental susceptibility in driving neoplastic transformation.

topics.label: Methods for detecting carcinogens and assessing risk
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe the genomic, epidemiological, experimental, and risk-assessment approaches used to identify carcinogens and evaluate their effects.

topics.label: Lecture summary and conclusion
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic provides the concluding remarks and final summary of the lecture.
